112
00:11:49,576 --> 00:11:53,772
So, what I'm thinking is maybe,
if I really wanna make a difference,

113
00:11:53,774 --> 00:11:57,147
maybe I get involved
in a great non-profit and...

114
00:11:57,149 --> 00:12:00,182
and I just put journalism
on the back burner for a little while.

115
00:12:00,184 --> 00:12:01,465
That's a great idea.

116
00:12:01,897 --> 00:12:02,897
Yeah.

117
00:12:05,484 --> 00:12:08,454
Oh, my God. That family is...

118
00:12:08,456 --> 00:12:10,897
That one, they are so weird.

119
00:12:10,899 --> 00:12:15,361
The dad is a perv, and the son
always stares at my boobs.

120
00:12:15,363 --> 00:12:18,584
Well... not as weird as

121
00:12:18,586 --> 00:12:20,338
<i>What Ever Happened to Baby Jane?</i>
over here.

122
00:12:20,670 --> 00:12:22,741
- What?
- Yeah, well...

123
00:12:22,743 --> 00:12:25,374
She's coming...
she's coming over to the table.

124
00:12:25,376 --> 00:12:26,678
- Hi.
- Hi.

125
00:12:26,680 --> 00:12:28,999
You guys were really
good sports yesterday.

126
00:12:29,001 --> 00:12:30,412
How are you doing?

127
00:12:31,144 --> 00:12:34,212
I don't know. I...
I feel like I failed, but...

128
00:12:34,214 --> 00:12:36,147
Oh, no.

129
00:12:36,149 --> 00:12:38,000
- No.
- Yeah.

130
00:12:38,467 --> 00:12:42,330
When I saw my mother's ashes
hit the water, you know,

131
00:12:42,332 --> 00:12:45,681
I just, uh... It just reminded me of...

132
00:12:45,683 --> 00:12:49,220
of, you know, sprinkling fish food
in an aquarium.

133
00:12:49,222 --> 00:12:53,422
And I was just like,
"Oh, my God," you know?

134
00:12:53,424 --> 00:12:55,807
Am I feeding my mother to the fishes?

135
00:12:56,108 --> 00:13:00,905
You know? And is that
what she would've wanted?

136
00:13:03,625 --> 00:13:05,284
- Uh...
- Just...

137
00:13:07,853 --> 00:13:10,139
Hope you're enjoying your breakfast.

138
00:13:10,141 --> 00:13:12,459
Yeah. Get... uh, get some.

139
00:13:12,461 --> 00:13:14,036
I think I will.

140
00:13:26,135 --> 00:13:31,012
Paula, you're not still mad
about that whole Trevor thing, are you?

141
00:13:31,455 --> 00:13:33,103
No, not at all.

142
00:13:34,084 --> 00:13:38,235
Okay, 'cause if you like a guy,
you can tell me.

143
00:13:38,237 --> 00:13:40,030
Or whatever. You can trust me.

144
00:13:40,032 --> 00:13:42,863
I'm not gonna, like,
swoop him out from underneath you.

145
00:13:43,722 --> 00:13:45,698
Yeah, I... I trust you.

146
00:13:46,399 --> 00:13:50,054
Okay, 'cause Trevor was just like
this momentary lapse of judgment,

147
00:13:50,056 --> 00:13:52,814
and I've learned my lesson.

148
00:13:53,798 --> 00:13:55,214
Hey, girls.

149
00:13:56,276 --> 00:13:58,203
Did you get your backpack back?

150
00:14:00,598 --> 00:14:02,577
You left it on the beach the other day.

151
00:14:02,885 --> 00:14:05,089
I... I gave it to one of the beach boys.

152
00:14:05,781 --> 00:14:07,844
- You did?
- Yeah.

153
00:14:08,384 --> 00:14:12,463
I gave it to the one over there.
The one with the khaki face.

154
00:14:15,509 --> 00:14:16,679
Thank you.

155
00:14:32,392 --> 00:14:33,721
- Christie.
- Morning.

156
00:14:33,723 --> 00:14:34,723
Hi, ladies.

157
00:14:34,725 --> 00:14:35,803
- Hello.
- Hey.

158
00:14:37,040 --> 00:14:38,379
Looking good.

159
00:14:38,381 --> 00:14:40,076
Sir. Sir!

160
00:14:40,078 --> 00:14:41,470
Dude.

161
00:14:41,472 --> 00:14:44,041
Oh, aloha. How is everyone this morning?

162
00:14:44,603 --> 00:14:46,384
You have our backpack.

163
00:14:47,839 --> 00:14:48,839
It's a green backpack.

164
00:14:48,841 --> 00:14:50,592
You said yesterday
that you didn't have it,

165
00:14:50,594 --> 00:14:52,720
but he just said
that he gave it to you two days ago

166
00:14:52,722 --> 00:14:54,575
and then you put it
in the lost and found.

167
00:14:54,577 --> 00:14:56,748
Yeah, I'm pretty sure
it's in your office.

168
00:14:58,269 --> 00:15:01,825
A green backpack?
I... yes, I do remember that.

169
00:15:01,827 --> 00:15:05,128
I'll... I'll go to the office
and get it for you right away.

170
00:15:07,195 --> 00:15:09,272
I was thinking that maybe
if I miss journalism,

171
00:15:09,274 --> 00:15:11,891
- then I can just come back...
- Hey, man. Hey, man. Excuse...

172
00:15:12,740 --> 00:15:13,801
Hey!

173
00:15:14,303 --> 00:15:15,364
Shane.

174
00:15:16,730 --> 00:15:18,231
- This guy's a fucking puke.
- Shane.

175
00:15:18,233 --> 00:15:19,654
- Did you see that?
- Shane. Shane.

176
00:15:19,656 --> 00:15:20,825
He fully fucking ignored me.

177
00:15:20,827 --> 00:15:22,538
I'm trying to talk to you
about my future.

178
00:15:22,540 --> 00:15:23,541
I know.

179
00:15:25,533 --> 00:15:26,796
Okay, yup.

180
00:15:26,798 --> 00:15:28,715
What do you think of that idea?

181
00:15:29,056 --> 00:15:33,797
Um... I think it's, uh, good.
I think it's cool.

182
00:15:38,833 --> 00:15:41,481
This fucking guy. I'm sorry.
I gotta deal with this.

183
00:15:41,789 --> 00:15:42,794
This is...

184
00:15:43,655 --> 00:15:44,655
Dude?

185
00:16:03,555 --> 00:16:04,766
Oh, Mr. Patton, good morning.

186
00:16:04,768 --> 00:16:06,644
Did you not see me
in the restaurant just now?

187
00:16:06,646 --> 00:16:08,092
- I'm sorry?
- I'm waving to you, I'm shouting...

188
00:16:08,094 --> 00:16:10,095
- I know you saw me.
- I was sent to fetch a bag.

189
00:16:10,097 --> 00:16:12,271
You looked right at me
and you kept walking.

190
00:16:12,273 --> 00:16:14,170
My apologies. So sorry.

191
00:16:14,172 --> 00:16:16,229
Oh, how was your candlelit dinner
last night?

192
00:16:16,231 --> 00:16:18,297
Yeah, that's what I wanted
to talk to you about.

193
00:16:18,299 --> 00:16:20,778
Uh, it fucking blew, frankly.

194
00:16:20,780 --> 00:16:21,921
- Oh, no.
- Yeah.

195
00:16:21,923 --> 00:16:23,964
You put us on a boat with a crazy lady

196
00:16:23,966 --> 00:16:26,426
who was having some kind of
fucking memorial service.

197
00:16:26,428 --> 00:16:28,789
You knew!
You knew that she was out there

198
00:16:28,791 --> 00:16:31,452
to spread her dead mother's ashes
on the goddamn ocean.

199
00:16:31,454 --> 00:16:33,048
Oh, well, she might've mentioned that.

200
00:16:33,050 --> 00:16:35,626
I'm trying to do
a romantic gesture for my wife.

201
00:16:35,628 --> 00:16:38,971
I got a crazy lady who's having
some kind of fucking nervous breakdown.

202
00:16:38,973 --> 00:16:42,834
So no, it was not romantic.
It was a dumpster fire shit show!

203
00:16:42,836 --> 00:16:44,017
I had no idea.

204
00:16:44,019 --> 00:16:47,976
I'm sorry your vacation isn't
everything you'd hoped... so far.

205
00:16:47,978 --> 00:16:49,565
But the good news,

206
00:16:49,567 --> 00:16:52,763
there's an exciting surprise
you'll be receiving later today.

207
00:16:52,765 --> 00:16:54,684
What? We're gonna get in our room?

208
00:16:54,686 --> 00:16:56,174
- Unfortunately, no.
- Jesus.

209
00:16:56,176 --> 00:16:58,309
But I think this is really
gonna turn things around.

210
00:16:58,311 --> 00:16:59,815
Then I don't want it!

211
00:16:59,817 --> 00:17:03,530
I don't want a free massage.
I don't want cheap champagne.

212
00:17:04,227 --> 00:17:07,595
What I want is to speak to your boss.

213
00:17:08,652 --> 00:17:10,291
Well, I am the resort manager.

214
00:17:10,293 --> 00:17:13,653
Yeah, but you have a boss.
Who is your boss?

215
00:17:14,206 --> 00:17:17,253
Our general manager, Mr. Zeoli,
is at a conference this week.

216
00:17:17,255 --> 00:17:20,802
Yeah, I want to get in touch with him.
Can I have his number?

217
00:17:20,804 --> 00:17:21,804
I'll have him call you.

218
00:17:21,806 --> 00:17:25,494
No! No. I'm calling him.

219
00:17:26,623 --> 00:17:28,544
I will have someone bring you
his business card

220
00:17:28,546 --> 00:17:30,525
with his cell phone number to your room.

221
00:17:30,527 --> 00:17:32,766
And you can call him at your leisure.

222
00:17:32,768 --> 00:17:36,424
Good. This morning, please.

223
00:17:44,464 --> 00:17:46,416
Motherfucker!

224
00:18:09,631 --> 00:18:10,983
Shit!

225
00:18:26,865 --> 00:18:27,875
Okay.

226
00:18:28,318 --> 00:18:30,831
I'm gonna need somebody's phone today.

227
00:18:31,313 --> 00:18:32,985
I can't go another day without a phone.

228
00:18:32,987 --> 00:18:35,317
You had my phone all day yesterday.

229
00:18:35,775 --> 00:18:37,491
Okay, can I have it again?

230
00:18:37,493 --> 00:18:39,326
No. I need it.

231
00:18:41,363 --> 00:18:43,623
- Yeah, right.
- No way.

232
00:18:45,163 --> 00:18:46,290
Mom?

233
00:18:46,292 --> 00:18:49,664
Honey, I'd love to help,
but I need to have my phone.

234
00:18:49,666 --> 00:18:51,353
I'm getting calls from work.

235
00:18:51,678 --> 00:18:52,897
Okay.

236
00:18:53,513 --> 00:18:56,175
Okay, but you guys
are gonna regret this.

237
00:18:59,457 --> 00:19:02,644
Hey, remember we got scuba, bud.

238
00:19:02,646 --> 00:19:04,191
We should've let him bring a friend.

239
00:19:04,193 --> 00:19:05,415
He doesn't have any friends.

240
00:19:05,417 --> 00:19:08,191
Of course he does. Hiroki Takeuchi.

241
00:19:08,193 --> 00:19:10,227
Hiroki Takeuchi moved back to Japan.

242
00:19:10,654 --> 00:19:12,487
What? When?

243
00:19:12,489 --> 00:19:13,980
Like two years ago.

244
00:19:15,723 --> 00:19:16,904
Quinn!

245
00:19:17,746 --> 00:19:18,746
Who?

246
00:19:18,748 --> 00:19:19,987
All's well that ends well.

247
00:19:20,554 --> 00:19:21,741
Thank you.

248
00:19:22,466 --> 00:19:24,485
- Bye, Dad.
- Bye.

249
00:19:31,663 --> 00:19:33,346
Mr. Mossbacher.

250
00:19:35,178 --> 00:19:36,276
How are you?

251
00:19:39,200 --> 00:19:40,758
I'm a little hungover.

252
00:19:43,023 --> 00:19:44,347
But not too bad.

253
00:19:47,295 --> 00:19:48,686
Well, you look great.

254
00:19:51,845 --> 00:19:52,908
Thank you.

255
00:19:55,069 --> 00:19:56,359
So do you.

256
00:20:11,000 --> 00:20:12,676
Well, have a good one.

257
00:20:15,469 --> 00:20:16,837
I'll see you soon.

258
00:20:30,220 --> 00:20:32,443
Pardon me, so sorry.

259
00:20:32,445 --> 00:20:33,626
Thank you.

260
00:20:33,628 --> 00:20:35,478
- Tanya, hi.
- Oh.

261
00:20:35,480 --> 00:20:37,825
I thought you might enjoy
some peppermint tea

262
00:20:37,827 --> 00:20:39,953
- before your wrap.
- Oh, thank you.

263
00:20:39,955 --> 00:20:42,491
Of course. Good to see you.

264
00:20:47,203 --> 00:20:50,080
Yeah. Helps with... circulation.

265
00:20:51,436 --> 00:20:55,613
Yeah. I just love peppermint tea.

266
00:20:57,720 --> 00:20:58,722
It's good.

267
00:20:59,636 --> 00:21:02,640
I just really wanna thank you
for yesterday.

268
00:21:02,642 --> 00:21:06,232
And being there for me,
getting me to my room.

269
00:21:06,234 --> 00:21:07,744
I mean, I was a mess.

270
00:21:07,746 --> 00:21:08,985
You were fine.

271
00:21:08,987 --> 00:21:11,819
It would've been a hell of a lot worse
if you hadn't been there.

272
00:21:11,821 --> 00:21:17,061
You have, like, a really beautiful,
kind, and calming presence.

273
00:21:17,642 --> 00:21:19,691
Seriously, Belinda. I'm not kidding.

274
00:21:19,693 --> 00:21:22,154
You... you should have
your own wellness center.

275
00:21:22,156 --> 00:21:23,156
You should.

276
00:21:23,158 --> 00:21:25,160
Because you really know
what you're doing.

277
00:21:25,162 --> 00:21:26,865
That's really very sweet. Thank you.

278
00:21:26,867 --> 00:21:30,632
You just can't be behind the desk
at some hotel spa.

279
00:21:30,634 --> 00:21:32,791
You need to be in business for yourself.

280
00:21:33,180 --> 00:21:34,180
I know.

281
00:21:34,182 --> 00:21:38,116
Yeah, and hey, I'm someone
who can make that happen.

282
00:21:38,607 --> 00:21:41,298
You should really think about it.

283
00:21:43,770 --> 00:21:45,970
It's something I could use.

284
00:21:46,675 --> 00:21:49,304
You know, I could have a lot of fun too,

285
00:21:49,306 --> 00:21:52,447
and I could, you know,
even give you a couple ideas.

286
00:21:52,449 --> 00:21:55,591
You know,
the whole vision could be yours.

287
00:21:58,070 --> 00:22:02,173
I'm flattered.
And I'm very much interested.

288
00:22:02,175 --> 00:22:06,741
Hey, one sec. Yeah, um...
I, uh... I gotta have, um...

289
00:22:06,743 --> 00:22:08,496
You drink the peppermint tea for now,

290
00:22:08,498 --> 00:22:10,596
and, um, I wanna talk about this more,

291
00:22:10,598 --> 00:22:14,923
but I'll be way more clear
after my oxygen facial.

292
00:22:14,925 --> 00:22:16,426
Okay. All right.

293
00:22:18,662 --> 00:22:21,463
Let's get into business! Okay.

294
00:22:31,586 --> 00:22:32,823
What the fuck?

295
00:22:32,825 --> 00:22:35,496
The bong is here, the weed is here,
but the pills are gone.

296
00:22:35,498 --> 00:22:37,472
No. What about the K?

297
00:22:38,113 --> 00:22:39,866
Do you think that fucker took our stash?

298
00:22:39,868 --> 00:22:41,192
The Klonopin, Liv.

299
00:22:42,138 --> 00:22:43,192
How's it going?

300
00:22:51,063 --> 00:22:53,036
Hey, can I ask you girls a favor?

301
00:22:54,592 --> 00:22:57,245
Can you try to include Quinn
a little bit more

302
00:22:57,247 --> 00:22:59,602
in your voodoo ceremonies
and whatever else you do?

303
00:22:59,604 --> 00:23:02,171
Mom, he's scuba diving
in the kiddie pool.

304
00:23:02,173 --> 00:23:05,709
No, I know, just in general.
You know, I just...

305
00:23:05,711 --> 00:23:08,056
I don't think you appreciate
how tough things are

306
00:23:08,058 --> 00:23:10,519
for kids like Quinn right now.

307
00:23:10,521 --> 00:23:12,134
Why? Because of the Asperger's?

308
00:23:12,463 --> 00:23:14,781
He doesn't have Asperger's, Olivia.

309
00:23:15,244 --> 00:23:18,779
But he is a straight, white, young man.

310
00:23:18,781 --> 00:23:21,619
And nobody has any sympathy
for them right now.

311
00:23:21,621 --> 00:23:24,039
And I just feel like we should.

312
00:23:24,764 --> 00:23:27,997
Yeah, in a way,
they're the underdogs now.

313
00:23:29,119 --> 00:23:30,408
Go on.

314
00:23:30,410 --> 00:23:32,656
Well, for instance,
young guys like Quinn,

315
00:23:32,658 --> 00:23:34,159
who are just getting out of college,

316
00:23:34,161 --> 00:23:36,820
I don't care how incredibly
impressive they are,

317
00:23:36,822 --> 00:23:39,715
it is almost impossible for us
to hire them.

318
00:23:40,225 --> 00:23:42,459
Well, isn't that because up until now,

319
00:23:42,461 --> 00:23:44,419
they're the only people
that you've ever hired?

320
00:23:44,421 --> 00:23:46,266
Yeah, don't you have
enough of them on staff?

321
00:23:46,268 --> 00:23:47,453
Trust me, I get it.

322
00:23:47,455 --> 00:23:52,982
I'm just saying,
I understand how guys like Quinn

323
00:23:52,984 --> 00:23:55,939
can feel a little alienated
from the culture right now.

324
00:23:55,941 --> 00:23:57,525
Mom, cringe.

325
00:23:57,527 --> 00:23:59,961
And I don't think it's fair to him.

326
00:23:59,963 --> 00:24:01,610
Mom, cringe.

327
00:24:02,342 --> 00:24:04,851
Olivia, he's my son, okay?

328
00:24:06,059 --> 00:24:08,398
I think he's gonna be okay, Nicole.

329
00:24:08,995 --> 00:24:10,282
Thank you, Paula.

330
00:24:11,168 --> 00:24:13,438
Okay. Paula's meds are missing.

331
00:24:13,440 --> 00:24:15,702
And so we need to go find them.
It's urgent.

332
00:24:16,088 --> 00:24:18,089
She's not gonna have
like a seizure or something?

333
00:24:18,091 --> 00:24:20,129
If I keep sitting here.

334
00:24:36,269 --> 00:24:38,568
Now, I know you said
you didn't want my surprise,

335
00:24:38,570 --> 00:24:41,103
but I took the liberty
of bringing it anyway.

336
00:24:41,649 --> 00:24:42,745
What is it?

337
00:24:43,411 --> 00:24:44,440
Well...

338
00:24:47,080 --> 00:24:48,142
Ta-da!

339
00:24:48,144 --> 00:24:49,417
Mom.

340
00:24:49,419 --> 00:24:51,099
- Am I interrupting?
- Mom.

341
00:24:51,101 --> 00:24:52,656
I know it's only your honeymoon.

342
00:24:52,658 --> 00:24:54,716
What are you doing here? Hey!

343
00:24:54,718 --> 00:24:56,159
Aw.

344
00:24:56,464 --> 00:24:58,359
Listen, I know this isn't kosher,

345
00:24:58,361 --> 00:25:02,039
and I told him to keep it a secret
because I knew you would say no.

346
00:25:02,505 --> 00:25:04,591
Get outta here.
Come on, come on, come on, come on.

347
00:25:04,593 --> 00:25:06,404
Dinner reservation for three?

348
00:25:06,406 --> 00:25:07,406
Yeah.

349
00:25:08,097 --> 00:25:09,097
Rach.

350
00:25:09,099 --> 00:25:11,409
Surprise!

351
00:25:11,946 --> 00:25:14,389
Oh, my God.
Look at her face, poor thing.

352
00:25:14,391 --> 00:25:16,724
She's white as a sheet.

353
00:25:17,109 --> 00:25:19,983
Don't worry. I have my own room.

354
00:25:19,985 --> 00:25:22,846
And I'm here just one night,
maybe two nights.

355
00:25:22,848 --> 00:25:27,074
I'm crazy. I'm so sorry.
I'm totally crazy. I know.

356
00:25:27,076 --> 00:25:29,154
I was just so tense from the wedding

357
00:25:29,156 --> 00:25:31,773
and all the weeks leading up to it.
I know you were too.

358
00:25:32,468 --> 00:25:35,670
And then Cathy Clement...
I swear this was Cathy Clement's idea.

359
00:25:35,672 --> 00:25:38,214
She said, "We should do a spa week
at the Mauna Kea."

360
00:25:38,216 --> 00:25:40,346
And of course that sounded amazing.

361
00:25:40,348 --> 00:25:42,184
And then I talked to you
on the phone, honey,

362
00:25:42,186 --> 00:25:45,353
and you sounded so upset.
You had me worried.

363
00:25:45,355 --> 00:25:47,131
And I thought, you know,

364
00:25:47,133 --> 00:25:50,623
maybe I'll just pop over
and see you guys for a second

01:02:22,906 --> 01:02:25,866
like Olivia is a product of privilege

from people like Kai,</i>

Now?

833

<i>Kai's genuine, and he wants to do good,</i>

but he's kinda stuck in a predicament.

835
01:02:40,844 --> 01:02:41,979
<i>"Do I end up stealing</i>

836

<i>or do I let people take advantage
of my people and my land?"</i>

837

<i>She tries to make the argument
that thieving is just,</i>

839

<i>Her arguments kind of land with him.</i>

<i>it's an opportunity for Mark,
and he rises to it, he protects her.</i>

844
01:03:13,055 --> 01:03:14,916
<i>He becomes her superhero.</i>

845
01:03:16,270 --> 01:03:17,424
<i>I love it because</i>

01:03:17,426 --> 01:03:20,304
it's so messy and sloppy and

<i>really pivots their lives

848

What do we do? What do we do?

Call the police!

850

Okay!

851
01:03:28,757 --> 01:03:31,688
That's what was needed to pull them out

853
01:03:35,819 --> 01:03:43,443
I'm a very needy person,

854

<i>Tanya's not 20.
When you hit a certain age,</i>

855

856
01:03:49,084 --> 01:03:52,015
I want you to get out of here
and save yourself

'cause I'm just like a...

I'm like a dead end, you know?

No.

Okay.

<i>And I think that</i>

he is attracted to her,

<i>He likes that.</i>

<i>She gets a guy handed to her
that's sort of overly simple</i>

<i>and still has</i>

a hard time making it all work.

Shane, doesn't this remind you

<i>Armond, in the beginning,</i>

is doing his best to hold together

878

he realizes that he no longer has to be

her mother-in-law's telling her</i>

Kitty is very close to her son, Shane.

900
01:05:36,146 --> 01:05:39,273
<i>She just thinks that Rachel

901
01:05:39,275 --> 01:05:42,180
Be happy, Rachel. Okay?

902

904
01:05:48,682 --> 01:05:51,143

905

<i>I think that, sometimes,
you're vacationing,</i>

906
01:05:54,748 --> 01:05:56,859

of just being away

908
01:05:59,707 --> 01:06:03,296

that the vacation is also

909
01:06:03,298 --> 01:06:05,087

910
01:06:05,089 --> 01:06:07,467

911
01:06:07,469 --> 01:06:09,718
<i>and some of them are personal problems,</i>

912
01:06:09,720 --> 01:06:11,972
<i>and so there really is no escape.</i>

'cause the guy

Shane.

Shane?

Good, good, yeah.

428
00:34:46,127 --> 00:34:47,357

429
00:34:47,359 --> 00:34:50,071
Yeah. Actually, we're gonna go
to Honolulu tomorrow.

430

Yeah, spend the weekend together.

431

That is so nice.
Make sure to do some shopping.

432
00:34:53,951 --> 00:34:55,206
I know.

433

And then maybe Aspen,
you know, for a couple months,

434

you know, see how that goes.

What? Making big moves?
Good for you, Tanya.

436
00:35:03,186 --> 00:35:05,208
Anyway, we're gonna be
leaving early, and I...

437

I really just wanted to make sure
that I didn't miss you.

438
00:35:09,432 --> 00:35:14,286
Belinda, you're an amazing person.
You are.

439
00:35:14,288 --> 00:35:17,272
I mean, you've helped me so much.

440
00:35:17,845 --> 00:35:19,806
I was a mess.

441

I showed up here, and... and somehow,

442

to just jumpstart my life again.

443

And I don't think
I'm ever gonna be functional.

444

445

I'll be able to break some old patterns.

446

Definitely.

447

but I'm realizing I'm getting back
into this pattern again

451

and then I use my money to control them

452

453
00:36:09,244 --> 00:36:13,819
the last thing I need in my life
is another transactional relationship.

454
00:36:14,952 --> 00:36:19,425
You know, it's just...
it's not healthy for me,

455
00:36:20,449 --> 00:36:21,517
you know?

456

Anyway, I really,
I want you to know how grateful I am

459

My glasses... and...

Look, I don't know

481

Quinn.

482
00:41:50,405 --> 00:41:52,754
I don't wanna go home.

483

486

Okay. Honey,

we'll take more trips.
You know, we'll get out of the city.

I mean, maybe not camping,
but, you know.

492
00:42:11,824 --> 00:42:15,555
I'm going on a Hokule'a, period.

Hey, Quinn, you're 16, you're a minor.

494
00:42:22,069 --> 00:42:25,172
You're still ours,
and we want you home, okay?

495

496

You know what?

497

I think we should finally buy that boat.

498

No, we can be one

501

502

503
00:42:41,802 --> 00:42:45,802
Yeah, we could jet ski, water ski.
We can waterboard.

504

505

It's wakeboard.

506

507
00:42:52,112 --> 00:42:54,236
- Same thing.
- Wakeboard.

508
00:42:54,238 --> 00:42:55,458

509
00:42:55,460 --> 00:42:57,965
Everyone knows that... No, Mom.

510
00:43:22,826 --> 00:43:24,766

511

I mean, there is no problem,

Yeah, I guess.

513
00:43:34,365 --> 00:43:39,070

514
00:43:41,773 --> 00:43:43,620
I just feel...

When I'm with you, I feel just...

516

weirdly...

517

alone.

518
00:44:09,033 --> 00:44:10,054
Uh.

519

Okay.

521

00:44:51,882 --> 00:44:53,172

00:45:15,136 --> 00:45:17,127
Sure, sounds good. Coming right up.

Greg. Greg. Water?

534

538

539

Well...

540

541

Death...

542
00:46:55,261 --> 00:46:59,931

543

_

546

548

I'm gonna need a boat.</i>

554

562

563

<i>You said you were
gonna bring me that number.</i>

564
00:49:18,317 --> 00:49:20,205
<i>I'm calling him.</i>

565
00:50:29,983 --> 00:50:31,793
I fucked everything up.

566
00:50:35,865 --> 00:50:37,092
It's okay.

567
00:50:39,688 --> 00:50:41,026
It's okay.

568
00:52:09,888 --> 00:52:13,032
I mean, I was always gonna live life

569

Obviously.

572

But, like,

573

574

575
00:52:33,157 --> 00:52:34,947

576

And, you know,
I've never been the kind of person

577

I don't want that.

578
00:52:40,212 --> 00:52:43,418
But I know that I have to deal

579

And...

582
00:52:51,182 --> 00:52:54,131
It's... I'm just having a moment.

583
00:52:56,849 --> 00:53:00,275
I don't know. I just...

586

Shit.

590
00:55:14,898 --> 00:55:17,425
That's perfect.

591
00:56:00,515 --> 00:56:01,745
What the...

Oh, oh, fuck. Oh, oh, fuck.

603
00:57:18,261 --> 00:57:19,716
Oh, God.

604
00:57:20,726 --> 00:57:22,356
Oh, fuck.

605

Oh, fuck.

606
00:57:27,248 --> 00:57:28,395
Oh, Jesus Christ.

607
00:57:29,191 --> 00:57:31,575
Oh, fuck. I'm...

_

_

Mossbachers!

- They did.

Kai.

623
01:06:35,779 --> 01:06:38,075
<i>Paula and Olivia are in a crossroad
in their friendship.</i>

624
01:06:38,077 --> 01:06:39,752
<i>I think that Paula
absolutely feels like,</i>

625
01:06:39,754 --> 01:06:41,918
<i>"I don't think that you can
fully understand me</i>

626
01:06:41,920 --> 01:06:43,588
as a friend, and as a person,

627
01:06:43,590 --> 01:06:46,007
and as someone who's
experiencing and seeing

628
01:06:46,009 --> 01:06:47,339
things on a certain level."

629
01:06:47,341 --> 01:06:49,469
To Olivia, what Paula did was wrong,

630
01:06:49,471 --> 01:06:50,943
<i>and didn't make any sense.</i>

631
01:06:50,945 --> 01:06:54,016
My mom could've gotten... really hurt.

632
01:06:55,043 --> 01:06:56,759
Something bad could've happened.

633
01:06:57,061 --> 01:06:59,073
Something bad did happen.

634
01:06:59,075 --> 01:07:02,815
<i>The unlikely happy ending of the show
is that Mark and Nicole end up</i>

635
01:07:02,817 --> 01:07:05,639
in a good place in their marriage
and their relationship.

636
01:07:06,311 --> 01:07:09,482
This is why people go on vacation.

637
01:07:09,484 --> 01:07:14,170
<i>Even in their dysfunction,
they rely on each other so much</i>

638
01:07:14,172 --> 01:07:16,907
that I think both of them
would be lost without each other.

639
01:07:16,909 --> 01:07:19,628
There is hope there, and there is love,
and you can see it.

640
01:07:19,630 --> 01:07:20,917
And I was really glad that

641
01:07:20,919 --> 01:07:22,558
<i>that was part of the story.</i>

642
01:07:22,560 --> 01:07:24,839
<i>You look at Mark and Nicole,
and ultimately,</i>

643
01:07:24,841 --> 01:07:26,588
they remain in their structure.

644
01:07:26,590 --> 01:07:28,877
<i>Quinn decides to do the opposite.</i>

645
01:07:29,594 --> 01:07:31,297
<i>It's like a parent's greatest hope</i>

646
01:07:31,299 --> 01:07:33,050
<i>and then, ultimately,
their worst nightmare</i>

647
01:07:33,052 --> 01:07:35,682
<i>is that, like, this kid's gonna be free
of all of his screens</i>

648
01:07:35,684 --> 01:07:38,435
<i>and make friends, but the friends
are gonna want to take him</i>

649
01:07:38,437 --> 01:07:40,354
on a paddle boat to Fiji.

650
01:07:40,356 --> 01:07:43,636
- Hi.
- Hi.

651
01:07:44,806 --> 01:07:47,063
You were on fire last night.

652
01:07:48,060 --> 01:07:49,372
I was?

653
01:07:49,374 --> 01:07:51,817
Yeah, you were hilarious.

654
01:07:51,819 --> 01:07:55,826
<i>Tanya finds Greg,
and Greg is this window into life again,</i>

655
01:07:55,828 --> 01:07:58,467
into love and romance.

656
01:07:58,469 --> 01:08:01,373
But the irony is that something is not

657
01:08:01,375 --> 01:08:03,330
<i>totally healthy about Greg.</i>

658
01:08:05,039 --> 01:08:06,039
Greg...

659
01:08:06,041 --> 01:08:07,523
I'm okay.

660
01:08:07,525 --> 01:08:10,836
<i>Greg is really ill, he's terminally ill.</i>

661
01:08:10,838 --> 01:08:13,471
So he doesn't sweat the details of life.

662
01:08:13,473 --> 01:08:15,407
<i>He's just going with the flow.</i>

663
01:08:15,409 --> 01:08:18,761
<i>She ends up blowing off Belinda
because she's found the man</i>

664
01:08:18,763 --> 01:08:20,069
of her dreams.

665
01:08:20,071 --> 01:08:22,756
But the man of her dreams,
how long is he gonna last?

666
01:08:23,260 --> 01:08:25,274
About the business...

667
01:08:25,891 --> 01:08:28,057
I really need to think about it.

668
01:08:28,360 --> 01:08:30,650
<i>The essence of who they are</i>

669
01:08:30,652 --> 01:08:33,027
is good for both of them.

670
01:08:33,029 --> 01:08:34,814
<i>But someone like Tanya's so spoiled,</i>

671
01:08:34,816 --> 01:08:38,171
<i>she couldn't possibly understand
Belinda's hardship.</i>

672
01:08:38,173 --> 01:08:41,420
Anyway, I really... I want you to know

673
01:08:41,422 --> 01:08:47,370
how grateful I am,
and I want you... to have this.

674
01:08:49,683 --> 01:08:51,336
<i>I think she's being genuine,</i>

675
01:08:51,338 --> 01:08:53,844
<i>and because of her privilege,
she doesn't understand</i>

676
01:08:53,846 --> 01:08:56,136
that gratitude can be expressed
outside of money.

677
01:08:56,138 --> 01:08:58,820
Tanya can make a mess of her life
and other people's life,

678
01:08:58,822 --> 01:09:00,595
and just keep going, moving on.

679
01:09:05,880 --> 01:09:10,281
<i>Armond is definitely
partially responsible for his demise.</i>

680
01:09:10,283 --> 01:09:13,069
But it's the whole game
that these characters are playing into.

681
01:09:13,071 --> 01:09:15,657
<i>You know, that is... It creates tragedy.</i>

682
01:09:16,687 --> 01:09:18,125
Oh, God...

683
01:09:19,129 --> 01:09:20,759
Oh, fuck...

684
01:09:23,116 --> 01:09:24,945
Oh, fuck.

685
01:09:25,696 --> 01:09:26,832
Oh, Jesus Christ.

686
01:09:26,834 --> 01:09:29,999
<i>Shane thinks there's
a violent burglar in his room,</i>

687
01:09:30,001 --> 01:09:31,637
<i>and he's defending himself.</i>

688
01:09:31,639 --> 01:09:33,095
<i>People do bad things in this show,</i>

689
01:09:33,097 --> 01:09:36,296
but there's no absolute villain,
and there's no absolute hero.

690
01:09:36,298 --> 01:09:38,437
<i>Everyone makes
some questionable choices,</i>

691
01:09:38,439 --> 01:09:40,468
<i>and you get to see why they made them.</i>

692
01:09:40,470 --> 01:09:44,284
<i>It's the manifestation
of how Armond feels about his life.</i>

693
01:09:44,286 --> 01:09:47,224
<i>And these absurd requests,</i>

694
01:09:47,226 --> 01:09:48,766
and he ultimately dies over it.

695
01:09:49,148 --> 01:09:52,562
Could I live with myself
if I made this...

696
01:09:52,564 --> 01:09:54,185
Faustian bargain,

697
01:09:54,187 --> 01:09:57,696
where I just ended up
being someone's arm-candy

698
01:09:57,698 --> 01:09:59,525
for the rest of my life?

699
01:09:59,527 --> 01:10:01,108
You want my advice?

700
01:10:03,495 --> 01:10:04,495
I'm all out.

701
01:10:04,497 --> 01:10:06,681
<i>For Belinda, there is some resentment.</i>

702
01:10:06,683 --> 01:10:08,705
<i>Like, "You can wipe your tears away</i>

703
01:10:08,707 --> 01:10:10,873
with a Louis Vuitton handkerchief,

704
01:10:10,875 --> 01:10:14,242
and that is something
that I can't really give you

705
01:10:14,244 --> 01:10:15,920
any shoulder to cry on about."

706
01:10:15,922 --> 01:10:18,013
You always have more options
when you have money,

707
01:10:18,015 --> 01:10:21,437
<i>and that helps propel Rachel back
into the relationship.</i>

708
01:10:21,439 --> 01:10:25,215
<i>The lifestyle that Shane provides her,</i>

709
01:10:25,217 --> 01:10:28,351
<i>ultimately, is more seductive</i>

710
01:10:28,353 --> 01:10:30,145
than her own self-respect.

711
01:10:30,147 --> 01:10:32,600
I'm happy, I promise.

712
01:10:33,507 --> 01:10:35,404
I'll... I'll be happy.

713
01:10:35,406 --> 01:10:38,654
<i>I think there's a real sadness
to their story,</i>

714
01:10:38,656 --> 01:10:40,700
<i>and you can see the writing on the wall,</i>

715
01:10:40,702 --> 01:10:43,578
and see that this girl is, ultimately,

716
01:10:43,580 --> 01:10:46,706
not going to be happy,
but doesn't know what to do about it.

717
01:10:46,708 --> 01:10:49,687
<i>It's a very fraught time in the culture,</i>

718
01:10:49,689 --> 01:10:52,795
as far as gender and race and class,

719
01:10:52,797 --> 01:10:55,325
<i>and I felt like, if we're gonna do
a contemporary show,</i>

720
01:10:55,327 --> 01:10:58,137
<i>we need to touch on all of those ideas</i>

721
01:10:58,139 --> 01:11:01,926
<i>and have a diverse group of viewpoints.</i>

722
01:11:04,390 --> 01:11:07,460
_

You guys just really...

do you get service here?

Wow.

00:11:40,335 --> 00:11:41,646

125

00:11:50,553 --> 00:11:51,781

- Yeah.

138
00:12:13,661 --> 00:12:15,263

139

148

149

150

151
00:12:49,488 --> 00:12:51,657

152
00:12:51,739 --> 00:12:55,827
Beautiful hazel eyes. Wonderful smile.

153
00:12:55,911 --> 00:12:58,705
- You're very kind.
- You must be very popular.

154
00:13:00,331 --> 00:13:02,584
- All right, Dad.
- Ah.

155
00:13:02,667 --> 00:13:06,337
Anyway, we're here because
we're gonna visit the town

156
00:13:06,422 --> 00:13:07,840
- my grandmother's from.
- Oh!

157
00:13:07,922 --> 00:13:11,218
It's a little town,
uh, Testa dell'Acqua.

158
00:13:11,301 --> 00:13:12,970
Yeah, that sounds very special.

159
00:13:19,268 --> 00:13:22,311
Hopefully, um, we can

160
00:13:22,396 --> 00:13:23,938

161
00:13:24,022 --> 00:13:26,108

162

'Cause we definitely

Oh, you should come, Isabella.

164
00:13:30,361 --> 00:13:33,364
You could be our

- Dad.
- Hmm?

166
00:13:34,742 --> 00:13:36,576
Leave her alone. We'll

167
00:13:36,659 --> 00:13:37,994
Okay, thank you.

168
00:13:38,077 --> 00:13:39,830
Shall I show you how
to close the curtains?

169
00:13:39,912 --> 00:13:41,456
There's a button over there on the...

170
00:13:41,540 --> 00:13:42,808
That's okay. We'll figure it out.

171
00:13:42,832 --> 00:13:45,168
I'd like to know. Where
is this button, Isabella?

172
00:13:45,252 --> 00:13:48,213
Dad! I'm gonna help you find it, okay?

173
00:13:48,297 --> 00:13:51,300
- Thank you very, very much.
- Thank you. Thank you very much.

174
00:13:51,383 --> 00:13:53,092
- Thank you.
- You're very lovely.

175
00:13:53,177 --> 00:13:54,177
Thank you.

176
00:13:54,177 --> 00:13:56,305
They are lucky to have you working here.

177
00:13:56,388 --> 00:13:58,474
Be our translator...

178
00:14:00,057 --> 00:14:02,853
You slammed the door in
that poor girl's face!

179
00:14:02,936 --> 00:14:04,772
You were harassing her.

180
00:14:04,854 --> 00:14:08,108
- How? I was not.
- You kinda were. And farting.

181
00:14:09,276 --> 00:14:10,319
It's the Prosecco.

182
00:14:10,402 --> 00:14:11,879
Okay. Albie and I are
gonna go to our rooms.

183
00:14:11,903 --> 00:14:14,114
We'll come back for you in
a bit. You gonna be okay?

184
00:14:14,197 --> 00:14:15,615
- Uh...
- Great.

185
00:14:22,080 --> 00:14:24,999
Why did we do this?

186
00:14:25,082 --> 00:14:30,004
It's nice, Dad. It's a nice thing to do.

187
00:14:30,088 --> 00:14:32,715
I got a migraine. I'm gonna go lay down.

188
00:14:32,800 --> 00:14:36,887
Okay. Well, I'm probably
gonna head down to the pool.

189
00:14:36,970 --> 00:14:40,306
Um, and then what time did
you wanna meet up for...

190
00:15:02,245 --> 00:15:05,832
The most ancient art is 14th century.

191
00:15:05,916 --> 00:15:08,252
- Oh, my God. Really?
- Yeah. Oh.

192
00:15:08,335 --> 00:15:11,003
- Your missing husband is here.
- Oh!

193
00:15:11,839 --> 00:15:13,382
- Oh, ho!
- Hey.

194
00:15:14,007 --> 00:15:15,508
Hi!

195
00:15:15,591 --> 00:15:17,736
- How was the flight? Mm.
- I missed you so much.

196
00:15:19,137 --> 00:15:23,057
Hey, uh, yeah, you know I
texted you a bunch of times.

197
00:15:23,140 --> 00:15:24,350
And you never texted me back.

198
00:15:24,433 --> 00:15:25,978
I know, I know. I'm sorry.

199
00:15:26,061 --> 00:15:28,021
We just had a flare-up
at work, it was...

200
00:15:28,104 --> 00:15:30,523
Shall I show you your room, or...

201
00:15:30,606 --> 00:15:32,734
Oh. Yeah, definitely.

202
00:15:32,817 --> 00:15:34,485
What the hell is she doing here?

203
00:15:34,570 --> 00:15:35,571
What?

204
00:15:38,156 --> 00:15:40,951
Yeah, uh, well, look.

205
00:15:41,659 --> 00:15:42,786
I'm traveling by myself...

206
00:15:42,869 --> 00:15:45,288
You bring your assistant to
a vacation with your husband?

207
00:15:45,372 --> 00:15:48,457
Anything you need, I'll be there. Okay?

208
00:15:48,542 --> 00:15:50,269
Well, I just don't know

00:11:40,820 --> 00:11:42,610

117

118

123
00:12:11,901 --> 00:12:13,486

124
00:12:14,729 --> 00:12:18,312

125
00:12:20,234 --> 00:12:21,861
You want me to rent a Vespa?

126
00:12:21,866 --> 00:12:24,656
Then at sunset...

127
00:12:25,281 --> 00:12:27,821

128
00:12:27,825 --> 00:12:30,449

129
00:12:30,453 --> 00:12:35,558
And then we...
we drink lots of aperitivos,

130

131
00:12:40,773 --> 00:12:45,178

132
00:12:51,149 --> 00:12:52,317
... beautiful.

133
00:12:53,434 --> 00:12:55,353
Well, all right. Sounds good to me.

134
00:12:57,188 --> 00:12:58,394
Really?

135
00:12:58,398 --> 00:13:02,603
Sure. Whatever you want.
It's... it's your day to shine.

136
00:13:06,572 --> 00:13:09,029
So, your employer doesn't

137

138
00:13:13,955 --> 00:13:15,744

139
00:13:15,748 --> 00:13:18,768

140

We're walking

141

You should come.

142
00:13:23,464 --> 00:13:27,423

143

Not at all. When there's

144
00:13:30,471 --> 00:13:32,886

145
00:13:32,890 --> 00:13:35,931
Okay. Yes, no. You... you should come.

146
00:13:38,896 --> 00:13:41,566
- Right?
- Yeah. Yeah, absolutely.

147
00:13:43,651 --> 00:13:45,357
Hmm? Say yes.

148
00:13:45,361 --> 00:13:49,153
Yes. I'll come.

149
00:13:49,157 --> 00:13:51,254
All right, well we're gonna go
get him some clothes,

150
00:13:51,259 --> 00:13:53,574
but you wanna meet up in like two hours?

151
00:13:53,578 --> 00:13:55,242
Yeah, perfect. Just text us.

152
00:13:55,246 --> 00:13:56,910
- Bye.
- Bye.

153
00:13:58,166 --> 00:14:01,419
I can't believe how hot...

154
00:14:04,255 --> 00:14:06,044
Hey. What's going on?

155
00:14:06,048 --> 00:14:07,546
What's with the boner?

156
00:14:07,550 --> 00:14:08,797

158
00:14:12,638 --> 00:14:15,304
Oh.

159

160
00:14:18,102 --> 00:14:21,518

161
00:14:21,522 --> 00:14:23,979
You know I sometimes
get horny after I run.

162

Well, couldn't you have just waited

163

165

You don't like morning sex.

166
00:14:32,575 --> 00:14:34,531
What? I'm fine with it.

167
00:14:34,535 --> 00:14:36,992
Are you? You're not a morning person.

168

Well, I don't wake up

169
00:14:39,665 --> 00:14:40,788
that is true.

170
00:14:40,792 --> 00:14:43,165
Look, I just figured
I'd take care of it myself.

171
00:14:43,169 --> 00:14:44,666
Okay?

172
00:14:44,670 --> 00:14:48,199
- Well, did you?

173
00:14:48,850 --> 00:14:50,018
Do you want help?

174
00:14:51,060 --> 00:14:52,349
Now?

175
00:14:52,354 --> 00:14:53,435
Yeah.

176
00:14:53,440 --> 00:14:55,730
No, it... It's okay.
We can do that later.

177
00:14:55,735 --> 00:14:56,902
It's not a big deal.

178

So, Daphne and Cameron never fight!

179

- Because that's what they said.

180

is not real. It's like, yeah,

182

184

185

They act like they're

186

188

It's like you have to find them

189

190

It's like, I don't know,

She is so sweet. She's a sweet old lady.

198

But like, you're not threatened by her,

200
00:15:53,698 --> 00:15:55,654
Like, she can just be sweet Carmen,

Everybody compares themselves

Why are you criticizing me

00:16:12,550 --> 00:16:15,845

209

But it's just, like,
are these the kind of people

Like, people that can only talk about

What? I'm a snob? They're snobs.

I agree, 100 percent.

00:17:05,478 --> 00:17:08,435

252

Oh.

284
00:20:32,171 --> 00:20:33,849

286

288

290

00:20:50,712 --> 00:20:52,669

No, no, no. We... We

The other thing is,
I'm here with my father

303

304

305

306
00:21:56,852 --> 00:21:58,395

Venice is unbelievable.

So cool. I mean, that's living, honey.

313
00:22:25,589 --> 00:22:28,171

You have to go

Trust me.

- Yeah.

00:22:53,492 --> 00:22:54,948

00:22:54,952 --> 00:22:56,241

00:22:56,245 --> 00:22:57,492

Okay, so, you didn't go

Oh!

Harper has, like,

64
00:04:45,576 --> 00:04:47,620
- (MUSIC CONCLUDES)
- Ciao, Rocco.

65
00:04:47,704 --> 00:04:49,122
Ciao, Valentina.

66
00:04:49,205 --> 00:04:51,708
- ISABELLA: Ciao.
- VALENTINA: Ciao, Isabella.

67
00:05:02,844 --> 00:05:04,846
- (IN ENGLISH) Happy to take them off you.
- Thank you.

68
00:05:04,929 --> 00:05:06,806
(INDISTINCT CHATTER)

69
00:05:07,306 --> 00:05:11,019
(IN ITALIAN)

70
00:05:11,644 --> 00:05:12,645
No.

71
00:05:14,814 --> 00:05:15,815
Ah.

72
00:05:33,958 --> 00:05:35,209
DOMINIC DI GRASSO: Buongiorno.

73
00:05:35,293 --> 00:05:36,586
VALENTINA AND ISABELLA: Buongiorno.

74
00:05:36,669 --> 00:05:38,796
(IN ENGLISH) Hello. I was
hoping to buy a present

75
00:05:38,880 --> 00:05:41,299
for my wife today. Uh,
she couldn't make it,

76
00:05:41,382 --> 00:05:42,717
- unfortunately.
- ISABELLA: Hmm.

77
00:05:42,800 --> 00:05:44,552
Uh, maybe a nice piece of jewelry,

78
00:05:44,635 --> 00:05:46,471
so I was wondering if there's a store

79
00:05:46,554 --> 00:05:47,638
you'd recommend.

80
00:05:47,722 --> 00:05:49,515
No, I don't know.

81
00:05:49,599 --> 00:05:52,226
But you could, uh, walk along the corso,

82
00:05:52,310 --> 00:05:54,020
and you'll find something.

83
00:05:54,103 --> 00:05:56,981
There's a wonderful
store called Pancrazi.

84
00:05:57,065 --> 00:05:59,525
It's very near, and it's very nice.

85
00:05:59,609 --> 00:06:00,860
Great. Grazie.

86
00:06:00,943 --> 00:06:02,445
- You're welcome.
- Prego.

87
00:06:05,823 --> 00:06:06,908
Grazie.

88
00:06:06,991 --> 00:06:08,201
(IN ITALIAN)

89
00:06:14,123 --> 00:06:15,124
Ah.

90
00:06:17,043 --> 00:06:19,003
(INTRIGUING MUSIC PLAYING)

91
00:06:19,087 --> 00:06:20,713
Okay. Grazie mille.

92
00:06:20,797 --> 00:06:22,006
(CHUCKLES SOFTLY)

93
00:06:27,762 --> 00:06:31,265
(MUSIC CONTINUES)

94
00:06:37,480 --> 00:06:39,065
(INDISTINCT CHATTER)

95
00:06:44,821 --> 00:06:47,115
PORTIA: (IN ENGLISH) I'm
just gonna get some fruit...

96
00:06:47,198 --> 00:06:48,783
really quick. I'll be right back.

97
00:06:49,450 --> 00:06:50,535
Okay?

98
00:06:51,869 --> 00:06:54,205
- Okay.
- (MUSIC CONCLUDES)

99
00:06:54,288 --> 00:06:55,331
- Hey!
- PORTIA: Hey.

100
00:06:56,374 --> 00:06:57,708
ALBIE DI GRASSO: How'd you sleep?

101
00:06:57,792 --> 00:06:59,836
- Uh, not good.
- No?

102
00:06:59,919 --> 00:07:02,046
No. We... we really should've hung out.

103
00:07:02,130 --> 00:07:03,965
I'm sorry that I
was... (BREATHES DEEPLY)

104
00:07:04,048 --> 00:07:05,842
I don't know why...
Just... Last night was...

105
00:07:05,925 --> 00:07:09,011
No. It's... it's fine.
Don't... don't be sorry.

106
00:07:09,095 --> 00:07:12,932
Yeah. Uh, we should
definitely hang out today.

107
00:07:13,015 --> 00:07:15,685
Okay. Yeah. That'd be fun.

108
00:07:15,768 --> 00:07:18,062
Yeah, I... I just have to get out

109
00:07:18,146 --> 00:07:19,939
of babysitting, you know?

110
00:07:24,986 --> 00:07:26,487
It's been a lot.

111
00:07:26,571 --> 00:07:29,407
I just have to deal with
that. And then, um...

112
00:07:29,490 --> 00:07:32,410
Yeah, maybe we can, like,
plan something after breakfast.

113
00:07:32,493 --> 00:07:33,619
Okay. Good luck. (CHUCKLES)

114
00:07:33,703 --> 00:07:34,829
- Cool.
- ALBIE: Okay.

115
00:07:34,912 --> 00:07:36,622
- (CHUCKLES SOFTLY)
- ALBIE: See you in a bit. Bye.

116
00:07:40,835 --> 00:07:43,588
PORTIA: So, I know
I'm, like, on the clock,

117
00:07:43,671 --> 00:07:44,922
technically, for today.

118
00:07:45,006 --> 00:07:49,510
Uh, but I was just wondering
if... if it'd be okay with you

119
00:07:49,594 --> 00:07:53,347
if I just hung out with that
guy that I met here for a little?

120
00:07:53,431 --> 00:07:58,227
He's nice and smart. He
went to Stanford and...

121
00:07:59,020 --> 00:08:02,190
and he's not non-binary.

122
00:08:03,232 --> 00:08:05,318
Yeah, I just mess everything up.

123
00:08:05,401 --> 00:08:06,819
I feel like if I won the lottery,

124
00:08:06,903 --> 00:08:08,196
I'd throw away the ticket.

125
00:08:09,697 --> 00:08:11,574
So, I just feel like I...

126
00:08:11,657 --> 00:08:13,868
should give him a chance, you know?

127
00:08:16,370 --> 00:08:19,498
(EERIE MUSIC PLAYING)

128
00:08:25,129 --> 00:08:27,256
I don't know what's
going on with Greg...

129
00:08:27,340 --> 00:08:28,841
(PENSIVE MUSIC PLAYING)

130
00:08:28,925 --> 00:08:30,468
... but I think it's bullshit.

131
00:08:42,980 --> 00:08:46,525
- (SPEAKING ITALIAN)
- (MUSIC CONCLUDES)

132
00:08:47,276 --> 00:08:48,736
(IN ENGLISH) So chic.

133
00:08:48,819 --> 00:08:50,696
Oh, oh...

134
00:08:51,447 --> 00:08:52,740
Thank you.

135
00:08:52,823 --> 00:08:54,158
You have impeccable style.

136
00:08:54,242 --> 00:08:55,576
The moment I saw you last night,

137
00:08:55,660 --> 00:08:59,080
I said to Matteo, "Finally, a
glamorous woman in Taormina."

138
00:08:59,622 --> 00:09:00,623
Thank you.

139
00:09:00,706 --> 00:09:02,458
QUENTIN: Oh, it's just the color.

140
00:09:02,541 --> 00:09:04,210
All the women here
dress like they're going

141
00:09:04,293 --> 00:09:05,628
to a funeral on the beach.

142
00:09:05,711 --> 00:09:08,631
But you, thank God
you're here. (CHUCKLES)

143
00:09:08,714 --> 00:09:10,967
We're just going to breakfast.
Do you wanna join us?

144
00:09:11,050 --> 00:09:14,220
Oh, no, that's okay, 'cause we just ate.

145
00:09:14,303 --> 00:09:17,181
Do you think we might see
you at the beach club later?

146
00:09:17,890 --> 00:09:18,975
Oh, yeah,

147
00:09:19,058 --> 00:09:21,644
I... I've never been to
the beach club. Is it nice?

148
00:09:21,727 --> 00:09:25,106
Come down, have a cocktail.
We always get the best seats

149
00:09:25,189 --> 00:09:27,733
'cause Marco's an old
friend who looks after us.

150
00:09:28,359 --> 00:09:29,610
Are you English?

151
00:09:29,694 --> 00:09:30,694
- QUENTIN: Ah. I am.
- Oh.

152
00:09:30,695 --> 00:09:32,113
- QUENTIN: Yes, originally.
- (CHUCKLES)

153
00:09:32,196 --> 00:09:34,573
But I live here now in Palermo.

154
00:09:34,657 --> 00:09:36,701
We've got a couple of
friends staying in the hotel,

155
00:09:36,784 --> 00:09:39,578
so we took the boat 'round to meet them.

156
00:09:39,662 --> 00:09:41,247
You have a boat, huh?

157
00:09:41,330 --> 00:09:42,665
- Yes, come down.
- (CHUCKLES)

158
00:09:42,748 --> 00:09:44,292
Come see the boat.

159
00:09:44,375 --> 00:09:46,043
We'll save you two chairs.

160
00:09:47,169 --> 00:09:49,046
- See you later. I hope.
- (CHUCKLES)

161
00:09:49,130 --> 00:09:50,381
Bye-bye.

162
00:09:53,050 --> 00:09:54,510
Those guys are nice.

163
00:09:55,428 --> 00:10:00,016
(PENSIVE MUSIC PLAYING)

164
00:10:11,819 --> 00:10:13,112
(LUCIA SIGHING)

165
00:10:15,573 --> 00:10:16,574
(SNIFFLES)

166
00:10:18,284 --> 00:10:20,453
(IN ITALIAN)

167
00:10:25,041 --> 00:10:27,293
- (MUSIC FADES)
- (LUCIA BREATHES DEEPLY)

168
00:10:27,793 --> 00:10:29,003
(MIA SIGHS)

169
00:10:29,962 --> 00:10:30,963
Mia...

170
00:10:32,340 --> 00:10:33,424
(MIA SIGHS)

171
00:10:48,689 --> 00:10:49,732
(CHUCKLES)

172
00:10:54,278 --> 00:10:56,280
No, no. Ah, Lucia. (SMACKS LIPS)

173
00:11:13,631 --> 00:11:14,673
(LUCIA SIGHS DEEPLY)

174
00:11:28,771 --> 00:11:30,439
Oh!

175
00:11:30,523 --> 00:11:32,400
- Luci.
- BERT DI GRASSO: (IN ENGLISH) Mount Etna.

176
00:11:32,483 --> 00:11:33,483
(IN ITALIAN)

177
00:11:33,484 --> 00:11:35,069
BERT: (IN ENGLISH) We should climb it.

178
00:11:35,152 --> 00:11:36,862
ALBIE: Not sure you're
up for that, Nonno.

179
00:11:36,863 --> 00:11:37,863
(IN ITALIAN)

180
00:11:37,863 --> 00:11:39,281
BERT: (IN ENGLISH) Yeah. I could do it.

181
00:11:39,365 --> 00:11:40,574
(INTRIGUING MUSIC PLAYING)

182
00:11:40,658 --> 00:11:42,159
That looks inviting. Let's try it.

183
00:11:42,243 --> 00:11:44,495
- Um, I'm gonna just... head back to the room...
- Come on!

184
00:11:44,578 --> 00:11:45,746
Have something with me.

185
00:11:45,830 --> 00:11:47,164
ALBIE: (SIGHS) I just ate.

186
00:11:47,248 --> 00:11:49,583
BERT: Well, perhaps you'll have a drink.

187
00:11:52,211 --> 00:11:54,380
LUCIA: (IN ITALIAN)

188
00:12:01,387 --> 00:12:03,180
- (MUSIC CONTINUES)
- (DOOR CLOSING)

189
00:12:06,475 --> 00:12:07,476
(GROANS)

190
00:12:09,437 --> 00:12:10,771
(SIGHS)

191
00:12:13,732 --> 00:12:16,902
- (SIGHS, BREATHES DEEPLY)
- (MUSIC CONCLUDES)

192
00:12:16,986 --> 00:12:18,320
(IN ENGLISH) Dude.

193
00:12:18,863 --> 00:12:20,781
Jesus Christ.

194
00:12:20,865 --> 00:12:23,117
- This is all your fault.
- (SIGHS)

195
00:12:24,285 --> 00:12:26,245
Come on. We had fun.

196
00:12:27,204 --> 00:12:28,372
(GROANS)

197
00:12:30,958 --> 00:12:32,042
Bro code?

198
00:12:33,085 --> 00:12:34,712
- ETHAN: Bro code?
- (CHUCKLES)

199
00:12:34,795 --> 00:12:36,172
Yeah, baby, bro code.

200
00:12:37,423 --> 00:12:39,842
Sure, yeah, whatever. Bro code.

201
00:12:40,926 --> 00:12:42,052
Thank you.

202
00:12:42,720 --> 00:12:43,720
I love you.

203
00:12:43,721 --> 00:12:45,848
- I just wanna be inside you.
- No, thank you.

204
00:12:45,931 --> 00:12:47,057
- CAMERON: Please.
- No, ma'am.

205
00:12:47,141 --> 00:12:48,350
CAMERON: I wanna do stuff to you.

206
00:12:48,434 --> 00:12:50,478
- No.
- I wanna make you feel good.

207
00:12:50,561 --> 00:12:52,021
(GENTLE MUSIC PLAYING)

208
00:12:52,104 --> 00:12:53,564
(ETHAN EXHALES DEEPLY)

209
00:12:53,647 --> 00:12:55,649
- Oh, fuck!
- CAMERON: You okay?

210
00:12:58,819 --> 00:12:59,904
(GAGS)

211
00:13:02,364 --> 00:13:05,951
(RETCHES)

212
00:13:06,035 --> 00:13:07,411
(EXHALES SHARPLY)

213
00:13:09,121 --> 00:13:10,206
You okay, buddy?

214
00:13:11,165 --> 00:13:15,211
(ETHAN RETCHES)

215
00:13:15,294 --> 00:13:18,631
- (MUSIC CONTINUES)
- (BIRDS CHIRPING)

216
00:13:33,646 --> 00:13:35,689
So, I was really high last night.

217
00:13:35,773 --> 00:13:38,484
Um, and I said a couple things I hope...

218
00:13:38,567 --> 00:13:39,693
(MUSIC FADES)

219
00:13:39,777 --> 00:13:41,028
... stay between us.

220
00:13:42,613 --> 00:13:44,031
Mm. You didn't say anything.

221
00:13:46,116 --> 00:13:49,328
I have trouble keeping
girlfriends sometimes. I mean,

222
00:13:49,411 --> 00:13:51,288
you know how girls are. (CHUCKLES)

223
00:13:51,372 --> 00:13:52,706
They pretend they wanna be your friend,

224
00:13:52,790 --> 00:13:54,542
but really they just wanna
get something out of you

225
00:13:54,625 --> 00:13:57,086
and then talk shit and
stab you in the back.

226
00:13:59,672 --> 00:14:01,131
But I feel like I can trust you.

227
00:14:03,509 --> 00:14:05,427
- Can I?
- (CHUCKLES SOFTLY)

228
00:14:07,096 --> 00:14:09,014
- For sure.
- (CHUCKLES)

229
00:14:12,518 --> 00:14:13,894
Plus, you don't know anybody.

230
00:14:15,145 --> 00:14:17,565
I mean, you don't know any
of the people that I know.

231
00:14:17,648 --> 00:14:18,899
(CHUCKLES)

232
00:14:19,984 --> 00:14:22,486
No. I mean, probably not.

233
00:14:24,363 --> 00:14:26,907
(INTRIGUING MUSIC PLAYING)

234
00:14:39,086 --> 00:14:40,129
Mia?

235
00:14:42,047 --> 00:14:43,048
Mia.

236
00:14:43,549 --> 00:14:45,593
(IN ITALIAN)

237
00:14:48,762 --> 00:14:50,639
- (MUSIC CONTINUES)
- Um...

238
00:14:50,723 --> 00:14:53,642
(IN ENGLISH) Portia says she's
heading down to the beach club.

239
00:14:53,726 --> 00:14:55,603
I might meet her there.

240
00:14:55,686 --> 00:14:57,813
Oh, your dad and I
can join you for lunch.

241
00:14:57,896 --> 00:14:59,732
Uh, maybe. I was kinda thinking

242
00:14:59,815 --> 00:15:02,651
of just having a day,
you know, for myself.

243
00:15:02,735 --> 00:15:04,445
I don't understand, you don't eat lunch?

244
00:15:04,528 --> 00:15:07,239
I think, let's just
play it by ear, yeah?

245
00:15:07,323 --> 00:15:09,033
- Yeah, all right.
- (CARD READER BEEPS)

246
00:15:11,368 --> 00:15:12,703
- (LUCIA GASPS)
- (SCREAMS)

247
00:15:12,786 --> 00:15:14,288
(YELLS) Uh... So... Sorry.

248
00:15:14,371 --> 00:15:16,165
- (MIA CHUCKLING)
- Sorry, wrong room!

249
00:15:16,248 --> 00:15:17,499
LUCIA: Yes!

250
00:15:17,583 --> 00:15:22,129
- (LAUGHS)
- ("PICCOLO PICCOLO" BY ROBERTINO PLAYING)

251
00:15:23,422 --> 00:15:25,883
I'm so sorry! We... We
thought it was our room!

252
00:15:25,966 --> 00:15:27,760
- Arrivederci.
- We are sorry.

253
00:15:27,843 --> 00:15:29,011
Buona giornata!

254
00:15:29,094 --> 00:15:30,095
(MIA LAUGHING)

255
00:15:31,221 --> 00:15:33,515
(SONG CONTINUES)

256
00:15:43,108 --> 00:15:45,986
(SPEAKING ITALIAN)

257
00:15:46,070 --> 00:15:48,989
(IN ENGLISH) That's the
weirdest voice I've ever heard.

258
00:15:49,073 --> 00:15:53,035
- Hey! Hi! So glad you came!
- Hello.

259
00:15:53,118 --> 00:15:54,662
Come back around and up.

260
00:15:58,957 --> 00:15:59,958
Okay.

261
00:16:00,042 --> 00:16:04,838
(INDISTINCT CHATTER AND LAUGHTER)

262
00:16:04,922 --> 00:16:06,882
Bellissima. Sorry, I'm already drunk.

263
00:16:06,965 --> 00:16:09,051
- (TANYA MCQUOID-HUNT CHUCKLES)
- QUENTIN: Hello. (KISSES)

264
00:16:09,134 --> 00:16:10,678
What can I get you to drink?

265
00:16:10,761 --> 00:16:12,179
Wow, yeah. Um, okay.

266
00:16:12,262 --> 00:16:13,889
- All right here. Okay.
- (CHUCKLES)

267
00:16:13,972 --> 00:16:15,641
I'm gonna have some
rosé if you have it.

268
00:16:15,724 --> 00:16:16,809
- Rosé?
- TANYA: Yeah.

269
00:16:16,892 --> 00:16:18,644
(SPEAKING ITALIAN)

270
00:16:18,727 --> 00:16:19,853
(RESPONDS IN ITALIAN)

271
00:16:19,937 --> 00:16:21,730
(IN ENGLISH) So, you've met Matteo

272
00:16:21,814 --> 00:16:23,357
and these are our friends
in for the weekend...

273
00:16:23,440 --> 00:16:24,650
- Oh, hi.
- ... Hugo and Didier.

274
00:16:24,733 --> 00:16:25,733
- Hello.
- Hey.

275
00:16:25,776 --> 00:16:27,778
- Bonjour, bonjour, bonjour.
- TANYA: Hi.

276
00:16:27,861 --> 00:16:29,655
- You're French, right?
- DIDIER: Yes! (KISSES)

277
00:16:29,738 --> 00:16:31,699
- Oh, my gosh.
- (DIDIER CHUCKLES)

278
00:16:31,782 --> 00:16:34,368
Didier's family have the most
incredible family estate in Èze,

279
00:16:34,451 --> 00:16:36,078
which you have to see before it crumbles

280
00:16:36,161 --> 00:16:37,579
entirely to the ground.

281
00:16:37,663 --> 00:16:41,250
It is my masterpiece
but it's ruined my life.

282
00:16:41,333 --> 00:16:42,543
- Yes.
- TANYA: Of course, yeah.

283
00:16:42,626 --> 00:16:45,879
Yeah. Take it from me,
I know how that is. I do.

284
00:16:45,963 --> 00:16:47,256
- DIDIER: Yeah.
- Jack! Jack!

285
00:16:47,339 --> 00:16:49,758
This is my naughty nephew, Jack.

286
00:16:49,842 --> 00:16:51,468
All right, all right. Hello, hello.

287
00:16:51,552 --> 00:16:54,263
It's nice to meet you, darling. (KISSES)

288
00:16:54,346 --> 00:16:56,265
- PORTIA: Oh. (CHUCKLES)
- Oh, shit! I know you.

289
00:16:56,348 --> 00:16:57,766
You were by the pool last night.

290
00:16:57,850 --> 00:17:00,477
- I was. Yeah, um. Hi, again.
- JACK: Yeah.

291
00:17:00,561 --> 00:17:02,896
You been in it? It's not heated, is it?

292
00:17:02,980 --> 00:17:05,399
Um, I... I don't know.
I haven't been in it.

293
00:17:05,482 --> 00:17:08,110
Should we get some
panelle, some fritto misto?

294
00:17:08,193 --> 00:17:10,571
Finger food is always a must. Anyway...

295
00:17:10,654 --> 00:17:11,739
- Oh! Thank you.
- Oh, thank you.

296
00:17:12,156 --> 00:17:13,157
Thank you.

297
00:17:13,240 --> 00:17:14,324
- That's it!
- Let's go.

298
00:17:14,408 --> 00:17:15,492
- TANYA: Oh!
- Salute!

299
00:17:15,576 --> 00:17:17,911
ALL: Salute!

300
00:17:17,995 --> 00:17:20,831
("FACILE DA DIRE" BY
SACHA DISTEL PLAYING)

301
00:18:03,749 --> 00:18:07,169
- (SONG CONCLUDES)
- So, you're from America then?

302
00:18:07,252 --> 00:18:08,545
- (DRINK POURING)
- PORTIA: Yes.

303
00:18:08,629 --> 00:18:10,631
- I've never been.
- PORTIA: Really?

304
00:18:10,714 --> 00:18:12,508
- JACK: No, I ain't been to shit.
- Hm.

305
00:18:12,591 --> 00:18:16,011
I'm from Essex, so...
Well, I've been to Essex.

306
00:18:16,095 --> 00:18:18,055
(CHUCKLES)

00:29:02,913 --> 00:29:05,213
I wanna show you around the island.

333
00:29:05,282 --> 00:29:07,352

334
00:29:10,088 --> 00:29:14,293

335

336

337

338

What a life you have. I
mean, this boat, your villa...

339
00:29:45,957 --> 00:29:49,828
Oh, my God, everything
you have is a work of art.

340

So many incredible palazzi in Sicily

341

342

343

344

don't we, Didier, darling?

346
00:30:04,375 --> 00:30:06,976

347

348

349

350

Portia? Portia... I can't

00:31:32,229 --> 00:31:35,935

00:31:47,277 --> 00:31:49,614

401

- Oh, my God.

00:33:29,546 --> 00:33:31,513
Yeah. Uh, okay. Uh... You're gonna be...

I... I really feel like
we're just overthinking

- this whole thing. And...

00:33:37,455 --> 00:33:38,455
Sh...

Portia?

00:41:41,506 --> 00:41:42,674
Um...

- Um...

487
00:42:06,931 --> 00:42:07,931

00:42:18,610 --> 00:42:19,811

00:42:41,399 --> 00:42:42,562

00:42:43,100 --> 00:42:44,100

491
00:42:48,440 --> 00:42:49,608
Ciao.

492
00:42:53,377 --> 00:42:54,377
Rocco.

493
00:43:00,851 --> 00:43:02,654

494
00:43:06,190 --> 00:43:07,890
Sì.

495
00:43:24,508 --> 00:43:26,645
Sì.

00:43:37,256 --> 00:43:38,256
Um...

00:43:48,299 --> 00:43:50,035
Um...

Wha... Fu...

Can...

Uh...

Grazie. Grazie mille. Grazie!

597
00:52:25,216 --> 00:52:27,386

600

601

604

605

And although it's not why I did it,

606

00:53:20,204 --> 00:53:21,640
Sweet girl.

611

612

613

614

615

a natural reaction.

616

Our Achilles' heel is an Achilles' cock.

617
00:53:51,602 --> 00:53:53,973
It's like a... a Greek curse.

618
00:53:57,708 --> 00:54:02,478
Um, I wanna... Can I pass on
dinner tonight? I'm gonna...

619
00:54:02,547 --> 00:54:05,245
I love you. Thank you.

620

Love you.

621

Oh.

622

623
00:54:20,864 --> 00:54:25,537
Guys, I just wanted to say,
this has been an amazing trip.

624
00:54:26,370 --> 00:54:27,535
When some...

625
00:54:27,604 --> 00:54:29,637
... flunky in the housing office at Yale

626

E in the same dorm room,

627

who would've known that
all these years later,

628
00:54:34,779 --> 00:54:36,815

629
00:54:38,216 --> 00:54:39,618
I think that's pretty cool, man.

630
00:54:43,855 --> 00:54:48,123
And, Harper, it has been fantastic

631
00:54:48,192 --> 00:54:49,894

632
00:54:51,830 --> 00:54:52,831
And, baby...

633
00:54:54,032 --> 00:54:55,964
thanks for putting up with me.

634
00:54:56,033 --> 00:54:57,802
- I love you.
- I love you.

635
00:54:58,468 --> 00:55:00,572
Cheers, guys. To friendship.

636
00:55:01,706 --> 00:55:03,475
To travel. To the good life.

637
00:55:04,208 --> 00:55:05,273
- Cheers.
- Cheers.

638

639

Hmm.

646

647

648

649

Very, very.

650

651

I wanted you to have the

652

653

654

Aw.

655
00:56:55,619 --> 00:56:57,986
Well, whenever you're ready

657

Do I... Wait... But what about Didier

I mean, don't they have to

No, Didier and Hugo are

661

662

663

00:45:06,120 --> 00:45:08,414
I mean...

607
00:45:09,665 --> 00:45:11,541
I hated him for years,

608
00:45:11,542 --> 00:45:13,960
but of course now, we're very close.

609
00:45:16,463 --> 00:45:17,964
Really, Tim?

610
00:45:17,965 --> 00:45:19,799
All right.
I'm gonna call you right back.

611
00:45:19,800 --> 00:45:22,052
Stay there, okay? Don't move.

612
00:45:22,636 --> 00:45:23,887
Oh, God.

613
00:45:25,139 --> 00:45:27,349
- Ugh.
- I gotta take this.

614
00:45:27,808 --> 00:45:28,892
Okay.

615
00:45:43,782 --> 00:45:46,160
So, what about the two of you?
Where'd you meet?

616
00:45:48,120 --> 00:45:50,580
Uh, in Dubai.

617
00:45:50,581 --> 00:45:53,666
Mm-hmm. Through a matchmaking service.

618
00:45:53,667 --> 00:45:55,001
- Matchmaking service?
- Mm-hmm.

619
00:45:55,002 --> 00:45:56,253
Wow, really?

620
00:45:57,921 --> 00:45:59,255
- Interesting.
- Yeah.

621

Yeah, I mean, we're different.
Different ages. I'm American.

622
00:46:03,594 --> 00:46:06,221
She's French. But we get along.

623

What are you talking about?

624
00:46:09,308 --> 00:46:11,351
- What?
- I'm not French.

625
00:46:13,812 --> 00:46:14,812
What do you mean?

626
00:46:14,813 --> 00:46:17,190
I'm from Quebec.
It's not the same thing.

627
00:46:17,191 --> 00:46:18,650
You know, I... I'm Canadian.

628
00:46:21,069 --> 00:46:23,322
French, French Canadian. Whatever.

629
00:46:23,822 --> 00:46:25,448
Whatever?

630
00:46:25,449 --> 00:46:27,533
I mean, there's only an ocean
between the two countries,

631
00:46:27,534 --> 00:46:28,618
but whatever.

632
00:46:28,619 --> 00:46:30,661
Okay, why do you have
to be such a stickler

633
00:46:30,662 --> 00:46:32,371
about everything? It's...

634
00:46:32,372 --> 00:46:34,207
- A stickler? Okay.
- French...

635
00:46:34,208 --> 00:46:36,375
I appreciate the geography
lesson, but, um...

636
00:46:36,376 --> 00:46:37,877
Well, clearly, you needed it.

637
00:46:37,878 --> 00:46:39,379
- What are you t...
- Okay.

638
00:47:15,791 --> 00:47:17,250
- Wow.
- Is he in a loincloth?

639
00:47:17,251 --> 00:47:19,378
Uh-huh.

640
00:48:11,263 --> 00:48:12,556
So pretty.

641
00:49:09,696 --> 00:49:12,531
Why is the Wall Street Journal
calling me, Kenny? Huh?

642
00:49:12,532 --> 00:49:14,743
I don't care about the fucking story!

643
00:49:15,911 --> 00:49:16,994
Why not?

644
00:49:16,995 --> 00:49:20,456
Because 20 agents
just raided my fucking office!

645
00:49:20,457 --> 00:49:23,542
- Fuck me, I'm done.
- Oh, sh... Is... Is it... Is...

646
00:49:23,543 --> 00:49:24,877
I'm gonna fucking kill myself.

647
00:49:24,878 --> 00:49:26,045
Just tell me what happened.

648
00:49:26,046 --> 00:49:28,047
I can't go to fucking prison. God.

649
00:49:28,048 --> 00:49:30,883
- Can you... Just...
- Fuck.

650
00:49:30,884 --> 00:49:32,426
You know, you told me
this couldn't happen.

651
00:49:32,427 --> 00:49:35,012
Remember that?

652
00:49:35,013 --> 00:49:38,015
You fucking swore
that this could not happen.

653
00:49:38,016 --> 00:49:39,684
I didn't think some whistleblower bitch

654
00:49:39,685 --> 00:49:42,229
in my office was gonna
rat me out to the media.

655
00:49:42,771 --> 00:49:44,563
Fucking FBI!

656
00:49:44,564 --> 00:49:46,816
- Fuck! Fuck me!
- All... all... all... all right.

657
00:49:46,817 --> 00:49:47,900
I just... Kenny.

658
00:49:47,901 --> 00:49:49,235
God, she did me so dirty.

659
00:49:49,236 --> 00:49:51,529
What exactly do they know?

660
00:49:51,530 --> 00:49:53,948
They have everything, Tim.

661
00:49:53,949 --> 00:49:55,741
- My accounts, my emails...
- Yeah, but what...

662
00:49:55,742 --> 00:49:57,660
- all the fucking documents.
- What did you tell them?

663
00:49:57,661 --> 00:49:59,830
- What did you say, Kenny?
- Nothing!

664
00:50:01,081 --> 00:50:02,416
I got a fucking lawyer.

665
00:50:03,709 --> 00:50:05,835
I should have never gone to Brunei.

666
00:50:05,836 --> 00:50:08,087
I should've never taken that position.

667
00:50:08,088 --> 00:50:09,839
Everybody was making a killing.

668
00:50:09,840 --> 00:50:11,424
- I figured, why not me?
- Kenny, Kenny.

669
00:50:11,425 --> 00:50:14,135
Kenny! Will you shut
the fuck up for one second?

670
00:50:14,136 --> 00:50:17,723
Just tell me. Am I implicated?

671
00:50:20,267 --> 00:50:23,061
Yes. For sure, Tim. Yes.

672
00:50:24,604 --> 00:50:26,605
What d... What... What...
What does that mean?

673
00:50:26,606 --> 00:50:29,859
Like... S... For... Yes?
That's a definite yes?

674
00:50:29,860 --> 00:50:31,402
That's why I bought this burner,

675
00:50:31,403 --> 00:50:32,695
to call you.

676
00:50:32,696 --> 00:50:35,156
You need to get a good lawyer,
like, yesterday.

677
00:50:35,157 --> 00:50:36,742
You've gotta be fucking kidding me.

678
00:50:37,492 --> 00:50:39,118
You know, this was a favor to you.

679
00:50:39,119 --> 00:50:40,703
Remember that? I didn't want to do it.

680
00:50:40,704 --> 00:50:42,788
This is all you. Now I'm wrapped up

681
00:50:42,789 --> 00:50:44,707
in some fucking money laundering,

682
00:50:44,708 --> 00:50:47,752

683
00:50:47,753 --> 00:50:49,086
And I only made ten million dollars

684
00:50:49,087 --> 00:50:52,465
out of your stupid fucking scheme. Fuck!

685
00:50:52,466 --> 00:50:55,593
What am I gonna do?

686
00:50:55,594 --> 00:50:58,179
I swear to God, Kenny,
if you fuck me on this,

687
00:50:58,180 --> 00:51:01,974
I will... I will kill you.
I will fucking kill you.

688
00:51:01,975 --> 00:51:03,101
You hear me?

689
00:51:03,953 --> 00:51:05,311
If it makes you feel any better,

690
00:51:05,312 --> 00:51:07,271
I'm gonna fucking kill myself!

691
00:51:07,272 --> 00:51:09,691
Good. You do it, you piece of shit.

692
00:51:22,120 --> 00:51:24,663
Bravo!

693
00:51:24,664 --> 00:51:26,665
- You're a legend!
- You're incredible.

694
00:51:26,666 --> 00:51:28,751
You are a legend. You are a legend.

695
00:51:28,752 --> 00:51:31,170
- So talented.
- Thank you.

696
00:51:31,171 --> 00:51:34,507
Well, once a performer
is always a performer.

697
00:51:34,508 --> 00:51:36,175
Do you agree?

698
00:51:36,176 --> 00:51:39,554
Yes! A hundred percent. We know that.

699
00:51:41,348 --> 00:51:43,474
Well, I'm leaving for Bangkok tomorrow.

700
00:51:43,475 --> 00:51:44,600
Oh, no!

701
00:51:44,601 --> 00:51:45,851
Yeah, if you need anything,

702
00:51:45,852 --> 00:51:48,479
- please let me know.
- Oh, you live in Bangkok?

703
00:51:48,480 --> 00:51:51,982
Yeah, my husband's there.
We come back and forth.

704
00:51:51,983 --> 00:51:55,236
Mm-hmm. He just got out of the hospital.

705
00:51:55,237 --> 00:51:57,071
- Oh.
- Oh, is he okay?

706
00:51:57,072 --> 00:51:59,990
Yeah. Last week, he had a stroke.

707
00:51:59,991 --> 00:52:01,075
- Oh my God.
- What?

708
00:52:01,076 --> 00:52:02,618
- He's had a few.
- Oh, no.

709
00:52:02,619 --> 00:52:04,703
- He's a fighter.
- Mm-hmm.

710
00:52:04,704 --> 00:52:06,748
He would love to meet you.

711
00:52:17,300 --> 00:52:18,884
- Awesome first day.
- Oh.

712
00:52:18,885 --> 00:52:20,886
- Oh, it was the best first day.
- It was the best day.

713
00:52:20,887 --> 00:52:22,221
- She was amazing though.
- Love you.

714
00:52:22,222 --> 00:52:23,472
Totally amazing.

715
00:52:24,558 --> 00:52:25,724
- You're amazing.
- Oh my God.

716
00:52:25,725 --> 00:52:27,853
Oh my God. Late night reading.

717
00:52:28,979 --> 00:52:32,168
- Look at this. Glowing. Sritala.
- Are you gonna...

718
00:52:32,170 --> 00:52:33,151
Are you gonna do it?

719
00:52:33,152 --> 00:52:35,401
Got my reading. Of
course I'm going to do it.

720
00:52:35,402 --> 00:52:36,486
I love it.

721
00:52:38,071 --> 00:52:41,240
- Love you!
- Love you! Give me the Cliffs Notes.

722
00:52:41,241 --> 00:52:43,117
- Ow, ow. Help me. Ow.
- Oh, gosh. Oh, gosh.

723
00:52:43,118 --> 00:52:44,869
You really should never wear heels.

724
00:52:44,870 --> 00:52:46,662
I know. I know. I know.

725
00:52:46,663 --> 00:52:50,458
- Oh, my gosh.
- Are you okay?

726
00:53:10,645 --> 00:53:14,524
Oh my gosh. Ooh, it's hot.

727
00:53:18,320 --> 00:53:19,945
She's so funny.

728
00:53:19,946 --> 00:53:23,867
Right? What a character.
A real Thai diva.

729
00:53:25,283 --> 00:53:28,286
No. No, no. I meant Jaclyn...

730
00:53:32,167 --> 00:53:33,710
So competitive.

731
00:53:35,003 --> 00:53:38,964
Well, you know,
she's always been like that.

732
00:53:38,965 --> 00:53:40,591
Yeah, but you'd think

734
00:53:44,387 --> 00:53:45,430
Narcissist.

735

A little bit.

736

And the vanity.

737
00:53:54,314 --> 00:53:55,814
I know she has to maintain it.

738

739

00:54:00,946 --> 00:54:05,659

741

742
00:54:11,998 --> 00:54:14,626
Gosh, she had the face everyone wanted.

743

I know.

744

And then the whole thing

745

Yes.

746

747

748

749

But I mean, are they ever

750
00:54:33,561 --> 00:54:35,522
I don't think they ever see each other.

751
00:54:36,606 --> 00:54:38,316
See? That's what I'm saying.

752

You know. I think she's lonely.

753
00:54:46,032 --> 00:54:47,700
- Really?
- Yeah.

754
00:54:47,701 --> 00:54:49,368

756

What?

757
00:54:53,540 --> 00:54:56,459
The bigger the front,

758
00:54:58,628 --> 00:54:59,629
Right.

759
00:55:51,598 --> 00:55:52,599
What?

760
00:55:54,851 --> 00:55:56,102

761
00:55:58,188 --> 00:55:59,230

762
00:56:02,442 --> 00:56:03,443
Protect me.

764

765
00:56:16,206 --> 00:56:17,374
She's a hooker.

766

767
00:56:20,752 --> 00:56:23,963
They met through
a matchmaking service in Dubai.

768
00:56:25,673 --> 00:56:27,299
She's a hooker.

769

770
00:56:32,180 --> 00:56:33,430
- Wow.

771
00:56:33,431 --> 00:56:34,973

773

774
00:56:38,395 --> 00:56:41,230
She's young and fun like me,

775

776
00:56:45,402 --> 00:56:47,946

777
00:56:52,575 --> 00:56:55,120

778
00:56:59,791 --> 00:57:01,793
I may have to go to Bangkok

779
00:57:04,838 --> 00:57:06,672
Bangkok? Why?

780
00:57:06,673 --> 00:57:08,216

781

782
00:57:14,013 --> 00:57:15,014
Don't worry about it.

783
00:57:21,312 --> 00:57:22,564

784

I'm not.

785
00:58:13,740 --> 00:58:16,117
Could you just get him

786
00:58:16,519 --> 00:58:17,784
He has all my numbers.

787

And may I ask

788
00:58:20,163 --> 00:58:23,665
Because I need a lawyer

789
00:58:23,666 --> 00:58:25,042
Of course. I will have him call you

790
00:58:25,043 --> 00:58:26,210

791
00:58:26,211 --> 00:58:28,462
- Okay.
- Okay? Thank you.

792
00:58:28,463 --> 00:58:29,881
Okay. Thank you.

793
00:58:33,301 --> 00:58:35,427
Anyway, so this one time when, you know,

794
00:58:35,428 --> 00:58:37,596

795
00:58:37,597 --> 00:58:40,766
there was this little girl,
and she had just learned

796
00:58:40,767 --> 00:58:42,893

797
00:58:42,894 --> 00:58:46,897

like, screaming to everyone,

798
00:58:46,898 --> 00:58:49,399
"Oh my God,
there's going to be a tsunami"

799
00:58:49,400 --> 00:58:51,151
But, you know, no one wanted
to believe her, but...

800
00:58:51,152 --> 00:58:53,278
- Was she like...
- They didn't listen to her.

801
00:58:53,279 --> 00:58:55,906
Yeah, well, so her dad comes down...

and their cousin's cousin,

393
00:27:08,752 --> 00:27:10,544
the fifth cousin, the sixth cousin.

394
00:27:10,545 --> 00:27:11,587
And the next thing you know,

395
00:27:11,588 --> 00:27:12,963
you have a military junta coming in,

396
00:27:12,964 --> 00:27:14,381
and they're taking the whole thing

397
00:27:14,382 --> 00:27:17,009
- right from underneath you. They're...
- I don't wanna cut you off.

398
00:27:17,010 --> 00:27:18,886
If I ever need help hiding money
from the government

399
00:27:18,887 --> 00:27:21,181
or my ex-wives, I'll call you.

400
00:27:21,848 --> 00:27:23,016
All right.

401
00:27:25,268 --> 00:27:26,353
Sawatdee, never.

402
00:27:31,399 --> 00:27:32,567
Bye.

403
00:27:34,069 --> 00:27:36,154
Thank you.

404
00:27:39,449 --> 00:27:42,076
So, are you two married?

405
00:27:42,077 --> 00:27:45,245
Nope, not yet, but we should be.

406
00:27:45,246 --> 00:27:47,748
You should put a ring on her finger.

407
00:27:47,749 --> 00:27:49,750
"It's on the table,"

408
00:27:49,751 --> 00:27:51,543
is what we say.

409
00:27:51,544 --> 00:27:55,507
You are all I need.

410
00:28:01,096 --> 00:28:03,306
How long is this boat ride?

411
00:28:06,893 --> 00:28:09,103
What's wrong with you?
You're acting strange.

412
00:28:09,104 --> 00:28:10,980
- No, I'm not.
- Yes, you are.

413
00:28:15,276 --> 00:28:18,196
So, what do you do, my friend?

414
00:28:20,115 --> 00:28:21,533
Oh, uh...

415
00:28:22,242 --> 00:28:23,284
What I do?

416
00:28:25,078 --> 00:28:28,664
- I do finance.
- Finance? That's exciting.

417
00:28:28,665 --> 00:28:30,250
How does finance treat you?

418
00:28:31,376 --> 00:28:34,461
Good. Yeah, I got a lot of big clients.

419
00:28:34,462 --> 00:28:35,838
- Uh...
- Do you?

420
00:28:35,839 --> 00:28:39,884
- I am a pillar of the community.
- Are you now?

421
00:28:42,345 --> 00:28:43,513
Oh yeah.

422
00:28:46,015 --> 00:28:50,395
My grandfather was the governor
of North Carolina.

423
00:28:51,521 --> 00:28:54,273
And my father was a...

424
00:28:54,274 --> 00:28:58,361
well, a very, very,
very successful businessman.

425
00:29:02,824 --> 00:29:03,991
Thank God he's dead.

426
00:29:05,744 --> 00:29:09,038
Oh, both my parents.
Thank God they are...

427
00:29:10,123 --> 00:29:12,834
...dead. Thank you.

428
00:29:15,253 --> 00:29:17,004
Mate, we are gonna go
and catch up with you

429
00:29:17,005 --> 00:29:18,505
at the bar.

430
00:29:18,506 --> 00:29:20,884
- Nice to meet you.
- Yeah. Yeah.

431
00:29:22,886 --> 00:29:23,928
Sure.

432
00:29:24,888 --> 00:29:25,972
Sure.

433
00:29:54,834 --> 00:29:56,335
I need you to focus really hard,

434
00:29:56,336 --> 00:29:57,377
- okay?
- Okay.

435
00:29:57,378 --> 00:29:59,380
And just think about your number.

436
00:30:00,006 --> 00:30:01,048
You thinking about it?

437
00:30:01,049 --> 00:30:02,132
- Mm-hmm.
- Promise?

438
00:30:02,133 --> 00:30:04,219
- Okay, 45?
- No.

439
00:30:04,844 --> 00:30:05,887
Shit.

440
00:30:07,096 --> 00:30:08,097
Um...

441
00:30:09,265 --> 00:30:10,724
do you wanna just check in your hands

442
00:30:10,725 --> 00:30:12,310
and see if there's maybe something...

443
00:30:14,062 --> 00:30:15,604
- What's that?
- Stop it! Are you kidding me?

444
00:30:15,605 --> 00:30:17,064
I don't... I don't know.
Where did that...

445
00:30:17,065 --> 00:30:18,857
- Where did that come from?
- Oh, no. That's my number.

446
00:30:18,858 --> 00:30:20,818
Come on! Get this kid a deck of cards.

447
00:30:20,819 --> 00:30:21,985
He can go all night, huh?

448
00:30:21,986 --> 00:30:23,529
That's crazy.

449
00:30:23,530 --> 00:30:24,613
He had to know. I mean, seriously.

450
00:30:24,614 --> 00:30:26,073
- I had three.
- How about we do this?

451
00:30:26,074 --> 00:30:27,616
- How about we...
- They weren't very strong.

452
00:30:27,617 --> 00:30:29,368
Why don't we just do some yoga...

453
00:30:29,369 --> 00:30:30,786
- No, I don't wanna do yoga.
- All right.

454
00:30:30,787 --> 00:30:33,247
- Then we'll give it a miss.
- I'm happy to just go to the bar, right?

455
00:30:35,250 --> 00:30:37,084
Why did you send us to that place?

456
00:30:38,586 --> 00:30:41,129
- You didn't like it?
- Didn't like it?

457
00:30:41,130 --> 00:30:43,841
That's not what we're looking for,
Valentin.

458
00:30:43,842 --> 00:30:45,801
We still have a buzz,
and the day is not over.

459
00:30:45,802 --> 00:30:47,804
You need to take us,
right now, somewhere fun.

460
00:30:48,596 --> 00:30:50,514
I don't think I can leave.

461
00:30:50,515 --> 00:30:52,808
You're our butler,
and we need your help.

462
00:30:52,809 --> 00:30:54,102
You are coming with us.

463
00:30:55,019 --> 00:30:57,104
He's coming with us.

464
00:30:57,105 --> 00:30:59,773
I... I can get a little crazy.

465
00:30:59,774 --> 00:31:01,775
We want crazy. We wanna party.

466
00:31:09,117 --> 00:31:10,159
Hold on.

467
00:31:23,506 --> 00:31:26,133
Hey. Mind if I join you?

468
00:31:26,134 --> 00:31:27,302
Hey.

469
00:31:30,430 --> 00:31:32,098
Mm.

470
00:31:39,939 --> 00:31:42,817
- Oh.
- Mm.

471
00:31:47,572 --> 00:31:48,698
Hey, Dad?

472
00:31:49,616 --> 00:31:50,699
Yeah?

473
00:31:50,700 --> 00:31:53,912
I just want to say thank you
for bringing us here.

474
00:31:55,455 --> 00:31:57,498
I know you've got a lot going on, and...

475
00:31:58,875 --> 00:32:00,710
and thank you for making an effort...

476
00:32:02,712 --> 00:32:04,088
